findings.reason: each newly claimed route needs a controlled prior-result/refresh case and an inline negative control to prove its request path no longer recomputes.
findings.text: The forced cold recompute and inline negative control exercise only `/_discover`; ten minutes of ordinary activity and a p95 latency can pass without forcing a refresh for `/_projects/index.json`, `/_checks`, or `/crew/velocity`

findings.reason: the stored-result identity and refresh inputs must include the normalized velocity query and its moving default window before this route can be served correctly.
findings.text: The three-function interface is keyed only by route and project, but `Handler._serve_velocity` in `reckon/serve.py` also varies its answer by `since`, `until`, `fields`, `limit`, and `cursor` (lines 3332–3350), with a clock-derived default window; two requests for one project can therefore receive the same stored answer for different questions

findings.reason: §5 must name the watcher or write-path caller that starts each child and move the stream and checks-summary derivations behind stored results; generalizing the existing child alone leaves the cited slow request paths in place.
findings.text: “Spawn on change” names no production caller for the generalized refresh: `_FleetChangeWatch` currently only invalidates and wakes streams (`reckon/serve.py` lines 525–526, 597–598), `_send_project_changes` still calls `discover_plans` inline (line 3276), and `/_checks` still calls `compliance.project_checks`, which walks every document in the request (lines 3762–3773; `reckon/compliance.py` lines 248–285)
